title: Continuity of the functor on localized sites
statement: Let $(D,K)$ and $(C,J)$ be small sites [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], and let $u:D\to C$ be continuous, meaning that precomposition carries sheaves of sets to sheaves. For every $V\in D$, the functor $u_V:D/V\to C/u(V)$ sending $(T,a)$ to $(u(T),u(a))$ is continuous for the localized Grothendieck topologies [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. No finite-limit hypothesis is required.

source.place: Tag 03CF, lemma-localize-morphism, first sentence of proof, via Tag 00Y1 fibres

proof.text: For a slice sheaf H on C/u(V), the fibre/extension equivalence writes H as the fibre of a map F to the sheafified representable of u(V). Use its explicit extension and invertible unit.

Pull F back by precomposition with u, and restrict to D/V. Both resulting ambient presheaves are sheaves by continuity and slice restriction. Their fibre consists of s such that p(s) is eta(u(a)). Naturality preserves this condition. A section locally satisfying the condition satisfies it globally by separatedness of the pulled-back sheafified representable, so Subfunctor.isSheaf_iff proves that this fibre is a sheaf.

source.place: Tag 03CF, lemma-localize-morphism, continuity sentence; explicit fibre verification

proof.text: Whisker the invertible unit of the fibre/extension equivalence by u_V. This identifies precomposition of H with the fibre just proved to be a sheaf. Sheafness is invariant under this presheaf isomorphism, which is precisely continuity.
